name: Baangi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: only Blench n.d. and McGill 2009/2012 Kambari classification notes/wordlists; no description of Baangi located

sources.citation: Buttacavoli, Ryan. 2022. A Phonological Sketch of the Tsuvaɗi Language with a Focus on the Tsudugu Dialect. Jos: SIL Nigeria. 77 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Sister language (Tsuvadi) only; names Baangi as a neighbour / East Kambaric member; no Baangi data; no stress statement for Tsuvadi either (two level tones + HL contour).

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Andrew Lewinan, Benard Abraham, Fittokka Gobak & Luther Hon. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Baangi [bqx] Language of Niger State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-060. Dallas: SIL International. 46 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 7.3 'Phonetic inventories' (printed pp. 11-13, pp. 17-19) gives tentative consonant/vowel tables only; Appendix C (printed p. 30, p. 36): 'The transcriptions are preliminary since no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features was conducted.' Wordlist carries tone diacritics; 'stress'/'accent' occur nowhere in the text. Sec. 5 (p. 5): 'Little research has been done specifically on Baangi.' downloaded from the Internet Archive (live SIL PDF behind an automated-access block).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2020 [ed. IV, 2019]. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry *Baangi, p. 53.
sources.note: Nothing. Entry gives names (ciBaangi, vuBaangi/aBaangi, Bangawa), Kontagora LGA / Ukata, >5,000 (1989), 'Source(s) Blench 1989' -- no grammar, phonology or dictionary cited.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. 2012. The Kainji languages of Northwestern and Central Nigeria. Circulation draft, May 2012, 369 pp. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.note: Nothing for Baangi or any Kambari lect. Table 4 (p. 10) lists Bangawa = vuBaangi/aBaangi/ciBaangi; Fig. 3 puts ciBaangi in Kambari I; wordlist-source table p. 40 gives 'Baangi -- Blench' (his own unpublished list); ciBaangi rows in the comparative wordlist; sec. 4.3 Kambari phonology (p. 32) consists of empty stubs. The string 'stress' occurs nowhere.

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart & Roger Blench. 2012. Documentation, development, and ideology in the northwestern Kainji languages. Language Documentation and Description 11: 90-135.
sources.note: Nothing. Table 3 (p. 99) lists documentation of Kambari lects: 'Cibaangi -- KJ700' (a Kainji survey wordlist only), versus theses/dictionaries for Cicipu, Cishingini, Tsikimba.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2010/2011. The Kambari languages (web page KmbOP.htm, rogerblench.info).
sources.note: Nothing. Classification table (Bangawa = vuBaangi/aBaangi/ciBaangi, Kambari I); the only linked document is a TsuVadi wordlist; no Baangi file.

sources.citation: Stark, Janie P. 2010. Kambari Orthography Design. SIL e-Books 16. Dallas: SIL International. xiv+227 pp.
sources.note: Baangi mentioned once (p. 30) as an 'exolect' of Kambari whose speakers 'deny being ethnically Kambari' (after Crozier & Blench 1992:64); no Baangi data. For Auna/Salka/Agwara Kambari: 'two level lexical tones', tone 'carries a very small semantic load' (sec. 2.3.1.5, pp. 61-63); 'Kambari is tonal' (p. 98). No word-stress statement anywhere (only 'Unstressed /u/' vowel-reduction note, p. 200).

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart. 2009. Gender and person agreement in Cicipu discourse. PhD thesis, SOAS.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing on Baangi: ciBaangi appears only in the Kambari subclassification figure (Kambari I). The phonology chapter concerns Cicipu.

sources.citation: Kamoru, [?]. 2011. [Study of patterns of language loss in Benue-Congo languages of Nigeria, including Baangi] (cited in Decker et al. 2021, sec. 5).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other work Decker et al. name as treating Baangi; sociolinguistic, very unlikely to describe stress.

sources.citation: SIL Nigeria / McGill & Blench. c. 2011. Kainji survey wordlist 'KJ700' for Cibaangi (McGill & Blench 2012, LDD 11, Table 3, p. 99).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Listed as the sole documentation of Cibaangi in the Kainji documentation table; a raw wordlist, unlikely to state stress but the only other Baangi data.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 1989. Baangi (Bangawa) wordlist, Ukata, Kontagora LGA. Unpublished fieldnotes (cited as 'Source(s) Blench 1989' in the Atlas of Nigerian Languages 2020:53 and as 'Baangi -- Blench' in Blench & McGill 2012:40).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only primary lexical data on Baangi other than the 2021 survey; tone-marked wordlists sometimes carry a prosody note. Never posted online.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. n.d. The West Kainji Languages of Northwestern Nigeria. Unpublished manuscript, 243 pp. (Glottolog ref 66310; language code includes Baangi [bqx]).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only Glottolog reference covering Baangi besides the survey; contains Blench's Baangi wordlist and possibly phonology notes. Probably superseded by the 2012 Blench & McGill draft (Kambari phonology stubs empty), so low odds of a stress statement.

sources.citation: Ajayi, [prob. Akinloluwa Irawomitan; first author of the citing dictionary, Dept. of Linguistics and African Languages, Obafemi Awolowo University per ORCID 0009-0002-4982-6535]. 2025. [Description of the sound system of Baangi; title, genre and venue not seen]. Cited in Ajayi, Ogunremi & Bamidele 2026, Baangi Dictionary (doi:10.13140/RG.2.2.18199.53929), front matter: 'Ajayi (2025) provides the first description of the sound system of Baangi'.
sources.tag: likely states tone; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists at the publisher (DOI recorded); open or paywalled, not checked
sources.note: Known only from the citing dictionary's front matter as relayed by search summaries: 'the first description of the sound system of Baangi' and the phonological analysis behind the dictionary's orthography; no record, abstract or text of the work itself was found (DataCite, Crossref, ORCID works list empty), so nothing about its tone analysis is known.
